title: Load a filled syringe into a syringe pump: flange in its slot, driver up to the plunger without pushing it
instruction: Load the filled syringe into the syringe pump. Lift the barrel clamp and swivel it away onto the handle, lay the syringe in the pump's cradle with the flange at the end of its barrel down in the flange slot, slide the grey plunger driver along its track until it is up against the end of the plunger without pushing the plunger in, then turn the barrel clamp back and lower it onto the barrel.
context: Loading a syringe pump is routine nursing work. Giving medications is a core duty of registered nurses (3.47 million in the US) and licensed practical nurses (667,000); O*NET 29-1141.00: "Administer medications to patients and monitor patients for reactions or side effects". Drugs that need a slow, exact rate go through syringe pumps, each loaded by hand. Medfusion 3500 quick reference card: "Lift the syringe barrel clamp and swivel it away", load the syringe with its flange "secure in the syringe barrel flange clip", "gently advance the plunger driver" until "it is flush", then "Turn and lower the barrel clamp onto the barrel of the syringe"; its manual: "The clamp holds the syringe barrel securely in place." PMDA (Japan) Medical Safety Information No. 50 reports a flange not in the slit, where "the set drug volume will not be injected". A driver that pushes the plunger in gives a dose nobody set.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A white syringe pump, fixed, centred at x 33, its cradle running along y: a white plastic body 5 cm wide (along x) and 2.35 cm tall, from y -5.5 to 4.45, with two white plastic rods 1 cm across and 2.8 cm apart (centre to centre) along its top, which the barrel rests between with its axis 3.98 cm up; the flange slot, 3.5 mm wide and reaching 14 mm below the seated barrel's lowest line, with a rounded mouth (5 mm radius), centred at y 5.125; past it, from y 5.8 to 14, the driver's track, and on it the grey plastic plunger driver (4 cm wide, 2 cm long, 3 cm tall, with a black grip 12 by 6 mm on top) that slides along y and starts with its face at y 11.85, 3 cm from the plunger. Behind the cradle, the barrel clamp: a grey post 8 mm across at x 37, y -2, rising out of a white housing 1.4 cm square and 2.35 cm tall; on it a white arm 1 cm wide and 6 mm thick reaching back over the cradle to a black pad 1.6 by 3 cm over the barrel's axis, and a black knob 1.4 cm across and 2.4 cm tall on the arm at the post. The clamp lifts up to 2 cm on its post against a light spring (with its own weight, 0.8 N on a barrel) and swivels a quarter turn toward the robot's right, its pad from over the cradle to over the handle; at the start it hangs down in the empty cradle, its pad 6 mm below where a barrel's top would be. The pump's handle: a white block 3 by 3 cm and 5 cm tall at x 37.1, y -6, under the swivelled pad. The syringe, a stand-in for a 60 mL syringe: a clear plastic barrel 29.6 mm across and 100 mm long with a nose at one end and at the other a flange 40 by 50 mm and 2.5 mm thick; 75 g. In it, a white plastic plunger (a rubber stopper, an 8 mm rod and a 30 mm square thumb disc, 12 g), pulled back full. The syringe lies on two black plastic stands (2 by 1 cm, 2.6 cm tall) at x 25, its barrel's centre at y -20, flange toward the pump (left).
scoring: The syringe is in the cradle when its barrel's nose end rests on the rods (the axis there within 3 mm of the cradle's centre line sideways, 2.5 mm of its seated height and 5 mm of its seated place along the cradle) and the barrel is within 15 degrees of the cradle's line. It is seated when the axis is within 1 mm of its seat (sideways and up), level and square to the cradle within 1.5 degrees, and the flange's centre is within 0.8 mm of the slot's (it has 0.5 mm a side). The plunger is in the barrel when its stopper is within 1 mm of the axis and its rod within 5 degrees of it. The barrel is clamped when the clamp is swung back over the cradle (within 5 degrees) with its pad down on the barrel's top (the post within 0.5 mm of that height) and not moving. The driver is near when its face is within 5 mm short of the thumb disc, and flush from 1 mm short of the disc to 0.2 mm into it (the contact's overlap in the simulator) with everything still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, the driver and clamp moving under 0.5 mm and 1 degree a step); a face more than 0.2 mm past the disc holds nothing and counts as not near. The plunger ever pushed in more than 1 mm or drawn back more than 3 mm, the plunger out of the barrel, or the syringe not in the cradle: 0. In the cradle, not seated (flange out of its slot, syringe cocked): 0.2. Seated and not clamped: 0.4, driver near 0.5, flush 0.6. Seated and clamped: 0.5, driver near 0.75, flush 0.9, and 1.0 once that has held for 1 s (the trial ends there). The plunger's travel is tracked through the whole trial, so a push or a pull undone later still scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0. To check a real trial: a side video for the flange in its slot, the clamp down on the barrel, the driver at the thumb disc and the plunger never moving off its graduation.
reset_notes: Pull the driver back to its start, lift the clamp, take the syringe out and lay it on its stands flange toward the pump, with the plunger pulled back full, then swing the clamp back over the empty cradle and let it down.
fidelity: Stand-in sizes for a 60 mL syringe. The barrel is 16 flat staves on two rods. The barrel clamp's sizes and light spring (the arm gives about 6 mm per newton) are stand-ins: measure them on the real pump. The stopper slides with little friction (a real one needs a firm push to start), so the scorer allows 1 mm of plunger travel from the driver's contact. The slot's mouth is rounded like a clip's lead-in. The driver slides without its release lever. Roll about the barrel's axis isn't scored.
